item.title: AI Study Tool Parses Courses and Tracks Skill Mastery Maps
item.description:
AI Study Tool Parses Courses and Tracks Skill Mastery Maps

🔍 Overview

An AI development tool has been released that allows users to upload various study materials, including lectures, web pages, screenshots, recordings, and Bilibili courses. The system automatically parses these inputs into searchable knowledge bases. It supports PDF, DOCX, TXT, Markdown, web pages, images, audio, and Bilibili/YouTube videos, requiring macOS, Python 3.12, uv, Node 20+, and ffmpeg.

🧩 How it works

The system processes different data types using specific methods:

  • Documents: Split by title hierarchy, preserving “Material > Chapter > Section” structure. PDFs are processed to remove duplicate headers, footers, and page numbers.
  • Web Pages: Prioritize the DeepSeek scraping interface, falling back to local parsing if it fails.
  • Images: Use macOS Vision to recognize Chinese text; if unrecognized, it attempts DeepSeek OCR.
  • Videos: Search for subtitles first. If missing, it uses local Whisper for transcription, extracts frames, performs OCR, and aligns explanations to pages to generate notes with timestamps and keyframes.
  • Ingestion: Recognized in batches of 20 pages. A failure in one batch does not affect others, and truncated pages are marked in the output.

From the materials, the tool extracts how knowledge points are tested, question formats, steps, pitfalls, and variations. If materials contain questions, they are automatically moved to the question bank and tagged with fine-grained labels. For example, specific topics like the “Cow Eating Grass” problem type are used for tagged question selection during exam generation.

📊 Skill Mastery and Practice

The tool generates exams by module with time limits, automatically grades them, and explains error reasons while updating mastery levels. A skill map displays the practice level of each section, with statuses including Proficient, Can Use, Understands, Unclear, and Needs Review. Weekly plans and reports are based on actual answering data rather than model fabrication.

  • Question Selection: Exams are grouped by subject, module, difficulty, and quantity. A default 30-question set includes 28 single-choice and 2 short-answer questions.
  • Answering Interface: Includes a countdown, answer sheet, and auto-save. When time expires, the paper is submitted automatically.
  • Reporting: Provides per-question analysis, scoring rubric hits, corresponding skills, mastery changes, and variation problems for practice.

⚙️ Key Details

  • Default System: Uses the “Peanut 13” system, categorizing materials into 8 major blocks (Material Analysis, Quantitative Relations, Verbal Understanding, Judgment Reasoning, Common Sense Judgment, Essay, Answering Strategy, Exam Planning) with over 200 skills.
  • Cost Tracking: Records invocation volume and costs for each model and provider. DeepSeek is calculated at official website prices (including peak/idle periods), while local Ollama is recorded as free.
  • No Key Mode: The workflow can be completed without an API key. Demo mode returns fixed academic, exam, and knowledge base answers. Document ingestion uses local hash vectors, requiring no Embedding Key.

📱 Availability and Requirements

  • iOS App: Built with native SwiftUI, minimum requirement iOS 17. Supports using Apple Pencil on a scratchpad for handwritten calculations during exams, saving one page per question for review after submission.
  • MacOS Requirements: Necessary for image OCR and iOS integration, though the backend is cross-platform.
  • Development Program: The 99 USD/year Developer Program only affects App Store listing and TestFlight distribution; it is not required for self-installing on devices.
  • Signing Limitations: Signatures expire after 7 days, requiring reconnection to a Mac to run. Supports a maximum of 3 devices with only 10 App IDs active at the same time.

#AI #StudyTools #MacOS #Whisper #SkillMastery

Source: yijiejiang/kaogong-school

item.title: Faster-Whisper Implements Whisper with CTranslate2 for Speed and Memory Efficiency
item.description:
Faster-Whisper Implements Whisper with CTranslate2 for Speed and Memory Efficiency

🔍 Overview

faster-whisper is a reimplementation of OpenAI’s Whisper model using CTranslate2, a fast inference engine for Transformer models. It delivers up to 4 times faster transcription than openai/whisper for the same accuracy while using less memory.

⚙️ Key Details

The implementation supports multiple precision formats and batch sizes, with significant performance gains. For example, transcribing 13 minutes of audio:

Implementation Precision Batch Size Time Memory Notes
openai/whisper fp16 5 2m23s 4708MB Baseline
whisper.cpp (Flash Attention) fp16 5 1m05s 4127MB Faster than baseline
transformers (SDPA) fp16 5 1m52s 4960MB Slower than baseline
faster-whisper fp16 5 1m03s 4525MB Faster and lower memory
faster-whisper (batch_size=8) fp16 5 17s 6090MB With batching
faster-whisper int8 5 59s 2926MB 8-bit quantization
faster-whisper (batch_size=8) int8 5 16s 4500MB With batching and quantization
transformers (SDPA) (batch_size=16) fp16 5 46m12s 14.801GB Slower with larger batch
faster-whisper (batch_size=16) fp16 5 25m50s 13.527GB Better with larger batch
openai/whisper fp32 5 6m58s 2335MB Full precision
whisper.cpp fp32 5 2m05s 1049MB Faster than baseline
whisper.cpp (OpenVINO) fp32 5 1m45s 1642MB Optimized inference
faster-whisper fp32 5 2m37s 2257MB Moderate speedup
faster-whisper (batch_size=8) fp32 5 1m06s 4230MB With batching
faster-whisper int8 5 1m42s 1477MB Lower memory usage

The efficiency can be further improved with 8-bit quantization on both CPU and GPU.

🚀 Availability

  • The module can be installed from PyPI: pip install faster-whisper
  • GPU execution requires the following NVIDIA libraries to be installed: cuBLAS for CUDA 12, cuDNN 9 for CUDA 12
  • The latest versions of ctranslate2 only support CUDA 12 and cuDNN 9
  • For CUDA 11 and cuDNN 8, the current workaround is downgrading to the 3.24.0 version of ctranslate2, for CUDA 12 and cuDNN 8, downgrade to the 4.4.0 version of ctranslate2

💡 Why it matters

Unlike openai-whisper, FFmpeg does not need to be installed on the system. The audio is decoded with the Python library PyAV which bundles the FFmpeg libraries in its package.

#whisper #ctranslate2 #speech-to-text #ai-inference #quantization

Source: SYSTRAN/faster-whisper

item.title: BuzzASR Introduces Fine-Tuned Whisper Models for 102 Languages
item.description:
BuzzASR Introduces Fine-Tuned Whisper Models for 102 Languages

Researchers have introduced BuzzASR, a collection of language-specialized fine-tuned Whisper models designed for automatic speech recognition (ASR) across 102 languages.

🔍 Overview

BuzzASR scales a simple fine-tuning approach to 102 languages covered in the FLEURS dataset. The development includes a language adaptation strategy that utilizes:

  • Monolingual tokenizer replacement
  • Data augmentation via text-only fine-tuning

⚙️ Key details

BuzzASR demonstrates significant performance improvements over Whisper-large-v3:

  • Language Performance: Outperforms Whisper-large-v3 on 77 of 102 languages.
  • Error Reduction: Reduces character error rates (CER) by an average factor of over 2.8.
  • State-of-the-Art Results: Achieves state-of-the-art CER among open-source systems on 27 of 102 languages when using the combined FLEURS and Common Voice test set.
  • Compression: The tokenizer replacement strategy provides an average 3.3x improvement in compression rate (characters per token) compared to Whisper’s multilingual BPE, with maximum gains reaching 21.7x.

🚀 Availability

All models, code, and detailed results have been released.

#ASR #Whisper #MachineLearning #OpenSource
